sections.label: THINKING
sections.content:
Now I see what happened! The UP action didn't move the blue rectangle - instead it changed the top bar (N/W colors) and moved one of the yellow shapes. The N bar shrank from 51 to 49 pixels, and the W bar grew from 13 to 15 pixels. Also one of the Y (yellow) shapes changed position.
Wait, looking more carefully at the Y nodes - in the BEFORE state there are two Y nodes (id=6 and id=7), and in the AFTER state there are also two Y nodes. But the "Differences" output says Y moved from one boundary to another - but that's comparing by color, and there are two Y objects. Let me look more carefully.
BEFORE:
- Y id=6: boundary=[[52, 16], [52, 19], [55, 19], [56, 20], [56, 23], [55, 24], [52, 24], [52, 27], [59, 27], [59, 16]]
- Y id=7: boundary=[[52, 40], [52, 43], [55, 43], [56, 44], [56, 47], [55, 48], [52, 48], [52, 51], [59, 51], [59, 40]]
AFTER:
- Y id=6: boundary=[[52, 16], [52, 19], [55, 19], [56, 20], [56, 23], [55, 24], [52, 24], [52, 27], [59, 27], [59, 16]]
- Y id=7: boundary=[[52, 40], [52, 43], [55, 43], [56, 44], [56, 47], [55, 48], [52, 48], [52, 51], [59, 51], [59, 40]]
Actually both Y nodes have the same boundaries before and after. The "Differences" output was misleading because it compared by color and found a mismatch due to ordering. The Y shapes didn't actually move.
So the only real changes were:
- N (green) bar: 51 pixels → 49 pixels (shrunk by 2)
- W (white) bar: 13 pixels → 15 pixels (grew by 2)
This confirms that the top bar is a HUD/timer that changes with each action. The UP action didn't move the blue rectangle at all - it just advanced the timer. This means UP is blocked from moving the blue rectangle.
So the blue rectangle can move RIGHT (and presumably LEFT and DOWN based on symmetry), but not UP. This makes sense if there's a ceiling or barrier above it.
Let me reconsider the goal. Maybe the blue rectangle needs to move to interact with the yellow shapes at the bottom, not the charcoal/magenta at the top. Or maybe SPACE does something special.
Let me try DOWN to see if the blue can move downward toward the yellow shapes.
